title: Compatibilities of purity for regular immersions
statement:
In the situation of [thm-pur-regular-immersion-purity], the purity
isomorphism is compatible with

1. *base change* along an étale morphism $X'\to X$, and more generally
along a smooth morphism $X'\to X$ of smooth $k$-schemes: then
$Z'=Z\times_XX'$ is smooth over $Z$, hence regular, and
$Z'\hookrightarrow X'$ is a regular closed immersion of the same pure
codimension $c$ (flat base change preserves regular sequences), so the
base-changed pair is again in the situation of
[thm-pur-regular-immersion-purity]. Base change along an arbitrary
morphism of pairs would leave that situation and is not claimed;
1. *transverse composition* of regular immersions: for
$i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ and $j:Y\hookrightarrow X$ transverse regular
immersions of codimensions $b$ and $d$, the purity isomorphisms for
$i$, $j$ and $ji$ compose with the twist additivity;
1. *cup products* (the purity class of a product of pairs is
the exterior product of the classes);
1. *finite reduction* from $A_{E,n}$ to $A_{E,n-1}$.

proof.text: Write $A=A_{E,n}$ and $T_W(r)=A_W(r)[2r]$. All functors and classes below are on the finite small pro-etale categories of [def-pur-conventions]. By [sk-thm-regular](a)--(c), the class $[Z\subset X]$ is characterized by its restrictions to frames, its exceptional adjoint $\operatorname{cl}_i:A_Z\to Ri^!T_X(c)$ is an isomorphism, and this very map equals the smooth-orientation composite $\Phi_i$ of [pur9-rg-def-phi]. Thus equality of supported classes gives equality of the corresponding purity maps; equality of these maps also gives equality of their twisted inverses. This fixes the normalization used in all four clauses.

source.place: Opening paragraph; normalization of all four clauses

proof.text: For a smooth $e:X'\to X$ of smooth $k$-schemes, put $Z'=Z\times_X X'$ and write $g:Z'\to Z$, $i':Z'\hookrightarrow X'$. As in [def-pur-regular-immersion], $X'$ is separated of finite type over $k$; $Z'$ is closed in $X'$, hence also. The structure maps of $X$ and $Z$ are smooth by [lem-pur-regular-immersion-smooth-structure]. Smoothness is preserved by base change and composition by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence], locally at each relative dimension. Hence $g$, $a_{X'}$ and $a_{Z'}$ are smooth. Smooth morphisms are flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. The schemes in question are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied over the spectrum of the field $k$ (a field has only the ideals $0,k$, hence is Noetherian). The flat-base-change and regularity assertions of [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus] show that the ideal of $i'$ is locally generated by a regular sequence of length $c$ and that $Z'$ (smooth over the regular $Z$) and $X'$ (smooth over $k$) are regular. Localizing at $z\in Z'$ (a flat localization, with nonzero quotient $\mathcal O_{Z',z}$) gives the pointwise regular sequences of [def-pur-regular-immersion]. Its dimension equality $\dim\mathcal O_{X',z}=\dim\mathcal O_{Z',z}+c$ is the dimension formula of [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus] for $f=i'$ on affine opens, factored as $\mathrm{id}\circ i'$ ($r=0$, equal residue fields, transcendence degree $0$). Consequently the purity theorem applies to the base-changed pair. This includes etale $e$, the relative-dimension-zero case.

source.place: (a), geometric hypotheses of smooth base change

proof.text: Choose a frame $(U,f)$ near a point of $Z$ as in [def-pur-frame-class]. Its pullback to $U'=X'\times_XU$ is a frame of $i'$: the closed subscheme cut out by the pulled-back functions is $Z'\times_{X'}U'$, since its affine ideal is the extension of $(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$. By [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality], pullback preserves the Kummer class of each $f_a$, its individual localization boundary, and the ordered supported cup product. Thus $e^*[Z\subset X]$ restricts on this pulled-back frame to $\prod_a\partial\kappa(e^*f_a)$, which is the restriction of $[Z'\subset X']$. Such frames cover $Z'$; the degree-zero sheaf and uniqueness assertion of [sk-thm-regular](a),(b) give $e^*[Z\subset X]=[Z'\subset X']$ globally. Passage to the purity maps: put $F=\Lambda_X(c)$, of etale origin through the root-sheaf identification of [def-pur-frame-class], and let $\beta:Lg^*Ri^!F[2c]\to Ri'^!Le^*F[2c]=Ri'^!\Lambda_{X'}(c)[2c]$ be the exceptional adjunct of the pulled-back counit composed with the inverse closed exchange; this is the base-change morphism of clause 1. Apply [lem-pur-closed-support-exceptional-mate] with $h=e$, $a=2c$, $\alpha=[Z\subset X]$, so that $u=\operatorname{cl}_i$ by [sk-thm-regular](c). Its last equation and supported-class identification, in the pro-etale form stated there, give that $\beta\circ Lg^*\operatorname{cl}_i$ is the exceptional adjunct of the supported-Hom class of $e^*\alpha=[Z'\subset X']$, i.e. $\beta\circ Lg^*\operatorname{cl}_i=\operatorname{cl}_{i'}$. Since $\operatorname{cl}_i$ and $\operatorname{cl}_{i'}$ are isomorphisms, so is $\beta$, and the same equation identifies the twisted inverse purity isomorphisms. No assertion that $a_{X'}$ is a base change of $a_X$ is used.

source.place: (a), frame calculation and passage to purity maps

proof.text:
For $Z\xrightarrow{i}Y\xrightarrow{j}X$ in clause 2, the clause speaks of the purity isomorphisms of $i$ and of $j$, so both pairs are in the situation of [thm-pur-regular-immersion-purity]: $Y$ is regular, and smooth over $k$ by [lem-pur-regular-immersion-smooth-structure] applied to $j$. Regular composition and codimension additivity follow from [lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus]; pointwise, $\dim\mathcal O_{X,z}=\dim\mathcal O_{Y,z}+d=\dim\mathcal O_{Z,z}+b+d$, and the concatenation of a regular sequence for $Y$ with lifts of one for $Z$ in $Y$ is regular. Hence $ji$ is also in that situation and all three purity maps are defined. Work componentwise, with $\dim X=N$, $\dim Y=M=N-d$ and $\dim Z=L=M-b$; these dimension equalities and smooth structure maps are [lem-pur-regular-immersion-smooth-structure]. Put $\omega_W=Ra_W^!A_k$ and let $\Pi_W:\omega_W\xrightarrow{\sim}T_W(\dim W)$ be the smooth orientations. Before cancelling twists, the three arrows underlying [pur9-rg-def-phi] are
$$q_i=(Ri^!\Pi_Y)c_{a_Y,i}\Pi_Z^{-1}:T_Z(L)\to Ri^!T_Y(M),\qquad q_j=(Rj^!\Pi_X)c_{a_X,j}\Pi_Y^{-1},$$
$$q_{ji}=(R(ji)^!\Pi_X)c_{a_X,ji}\Pi_Z^{-1}.$$
By [sk-thm-regular](c), cancelling $T_Z(L)$, $T_Y(M)$ or $T_Z(L)$ in these arrows gives exactly $\operatorname{cl}_i,\operatorname{cl}_j,\operatorname{cl}_{ji}$, respectively. The finite open-and-closed component assembly is the one specified in [pur9-rg-def-phi].

source.place: (b), specified orientation factors for the nested immersions

proof.text:
Expand $Ri^!(q_j)q_i$. Functoriality cancels the adjacent factors $Ri^!(\Pi_Y^{-1})Ri^!(\Pi_Y)=1$; naturality moves $Ri^!Rj^!(\Pi_X)$ to the front. Associativity of the specified exceptional compositors, [sk-thm-sf-compatibility](1), then gives
$$Ri^!(q_j)q_i=c_{j,i,T_X(N)}q_{ji}.$$
To cancel twists in this equation, apply [lem-pur-coprojection-composition-mate] with $(f,g)=(i,j)$ and with the invertible Tate shifts used in [pur9-rg-def-phi]. Its displayed equation says precisely that moving such a shift through $R(ji)^!$ agrees with first moving it through $Rj^!$ and then $Ri^!$. Its hypotheses hold: the arrows are separated finite type and the Tate lines are invertible finite-Tor objects by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free], with the twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. The cancelled equality is
$$\operatorname{cl}_{ji}=c_{j,i,T_X(b+d)}^{-1}\,Ri^!\bigl(\operatorname{cl}_j(b)[2b]\bigr)\,\operatorname{cl}_i,$$
where the middle arrow includes the inverse co-projection $\bigl(Rj^!T_X(d)\bigr)(b)[2b]\cong Rj^!T_X(b+d)$. This is the asserted composition law; taking twisted inverses gives its equivalent purity-isomorphism form. All shift degrees are even, so the tensor reassociations contribute no sign.

source.place: (b), cancellation of the middle orientation and composition of co-projections

proof.text: For products, [sk-thm-regular](d) states that the product pair $(X_1\times_kX_2,Z_1\times_kZ_2)$ is again in the situation of the theorem, of codimension $c_1+c_2$, and that $[Z_1\times Z_2\subset X_1\times X_2]=[Z_1\subset X_1]\boxtimes[Z_2\subset X_2]$ under the exterior product of classes with supports. This is the class form of clause 3; by [sk-thm-regular](a),(c) each class map $\operatorname{cl}$ is the unique map from the unit sending $1$ to the class, so the purity maps of the product pair are determined by this exterior product. This is a product-frame statement; it does not deduce a nested-composition formula from supported Kunneth.

For finite reduction assume $n\geq2$, put $B=A_{E,n-1}$ and $S_W=-\otimes^L_A B$. Use the finite-reduction comparisons for the actual operations in [sk-thm-sf-compatibility](7); they preserve composition maps, adjunctions and projection maps. In particular they preserve the co-projection, since it is the adjunction conjugate of projection with an inverse Tate line, as specified by [lem-pur-coprojection-composition-mate]. The Tate shifts reduce to $B_W(r)[2r]$ by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] and the twist definition [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Smooth purity of $a_X,a_Z$ commutes with $S$ by [thm-pur-finite-reduction-of-purity]. Apply $S$ to the three factors defining $q_i=(Ri^!\Pi_X)c_{a_X,i}\Pi_Z^{-1}$. Under the specified comparisons each factor becomes the corresponding $B$-coefficient factor; functors preserve inverses, so
$$S_Z(q_i)=(Ri_B^!\Pi_{X,B})c^B_{a_X,i}\Pi_{Z,B}^{-1}.$$
The same co-projection comparison therefore identifies $S_Z(\Phi_{i,A})$ with $\Phi_{i,B}$. Finally [sk-thm-regular](c) identifies these maps with $\operatorname{cl}_{i,A}$ and $\operatorname{cl}_{i,B}$. This proves clause 4 for the specified purity maps and their inverses. All inputs are bounded constructible finite-Tor: Tate shifts are rank-one, and their exceptional images in this calculation are Tate shifts by purity. This uses derived reduction; it does not assume that $B$ is flat over $A$.

source.place: (d), coefficient reduction of the specified smooth-orientation factors

proof.text: If a support is empty, its degree-zero coefficient object and its supported class are zero, so the displayed identities are the unique identities between zero maps. If a component has codimension zero, use the empty frame product $1$ from [def-pur-frame-class]; the same formulas reduce to the unit laws of [sk-thm-sf-compatibility](1),(3). The component assemblies of [pur9-rg-def-phi] preserve every displayed equality, since those maps are characterized by their restrictions to the finite open-and-closed decomposition. Clause 4 makes no assertion at $n=1$, because the finite coefficient conventions start at level one.

source.place: All clauses, empty supports and componentwise assembly

In the situation of [thm-pur-regular-immersion-purity], the purity
isomorphism is compatible with

1. *base change* along an étale morphism $X'\to X$, and more generally
along a smooth morphism $X'\to X$ of smooth $k$-schemes: then
$Z'=Z\times_XX'$ is smooth over $Z$, hence regular, and
$Z'\hookrightarrow X'$ is a regular closed immersion of the same pure
codimension $c$ (flat base change preserves regular sequences), so the
base-changed pair is again in the situation of
[thm-pur-regular-immersion-purity]. Base change along an arbitrary
morphism of pairs would leave that situation and is not claimed;
1. *transverse composition* of regular immersions: for
$i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ and $j:Y\hookrightarrow X$ transverse regular
immersions of codimensions $b$ and $d$, the purity isomorphisms for
$i$, $j$ and $ji$ compose with the twist additivity;
1. *cup products* (the purity class of a product of pairs is

proof.text:
All four assertions reduce to the corresponding assertions about the
canonical classes of [def-pur-frame-class] together with the
canonical structure of the identification of
[thm-pur-regular-immersion-purity]: the purity isomorphism is
$(-1)^c$ times the composite of the smooth purity identifications of
the structure morphisms, the composition law for $(-)^!$ and the
co-projection (Steps 1–2 of [thm-pur-regular-immersion-purity]), and
only the classes carry the content (everything else is the canonical
six-functor structure). The sign $(-1)^c$ is preserved by base change
of the same codimension, multiplicative under transverse composition
and exterior products (the codimensions add) and unchanged by
reduction of the coefficients, so it is compatible with all four
assertions.

*(a) Base change.* For $X'\to X$ smooth (in particular étale) the structure morphisms and the whole
composite identification of Steps 1–2 are stable under base change
(the structure morphisms of the base-changed pair are the base changes
of the structure morphisms; the smooth purity identification
[thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] is compatible with base
change; the composition law and the co-projection are canonical); the
class of the pair is the Kummer boundary, whose
[lem-pur-frame-independence] and compatibility with pullback give
the assertion.

*(b) Transverse composition.* For transverse $i,j$, the frame
of $ji$ is the product of the frames of the two immersions (the ideal is generated by the ideal of $Y$ in $X$
and lifts of generators of the ideal of $Z$ in $Y$); the Kummer
class of the multiplication is the sum and the exterior product of the
classes of the two frames is the class of the composite pair by
[lem-pur-kunneth-supported]; combining with the twist additivity
of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] and the composition law for $(-)^!$
of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] gives the statement (the
dimensions add: $c=b+d$).

*(c) Cup products.* The canonical class of a product of pairs is
the exterior product of the classes, by [lem-pur-kunneth-supported]
and [lem-pur-frame-independence]; an iterated application gives
the cup-product compatibility.

*(d) Finite reduction.* The Kummer boundary of the coordinate
reduces to itself (the Kummer sequence is natural in $n$), the
localization triangles and the classes reduce compatibly by the
naturality of [lem-pur-kunneth-supported] and of the
recollement; hence every displayed step of
[thm-pur-regular-immersion-purity] is natural in $n$.
